title: 103. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Finding Constants of Direct Proportionality
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Constant of Direct Proportionality from a Pair of Values
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the constant of proportionality from a pair of directly proportional values.
questions.question: If \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\), and \(y=20\) when \(x=4\), what is the constant of proportionality?
questions.explanation: For direct proportion, \(y=kx\). Substitute \(y=20\) and \(x=4\): \(20=4k\). Dividing both sides by \(4\) gives \(k=5\). The alternative copies the given \(x\)-value instead of calculating \(\frac{y}{x}\).
questions.hint: Identify which variable is the output and which is the input.

questions.concept: Constant of Direct Proportionality from a Pair of Values
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the constant of proportionality from given directly proportional values.
questions.question: If \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\), and \(y=18\) when \(x=3\), what is the constant of proportionality?
questions.explanation: Since \(y=kx\), substitute \(y=18\) and \(x=3\): \(18=3k\). Dividing both sides by \(3\) gives \(k=6\). The alternative subtracts the values, \(18-3=15\), instead of dividing.
questions.hint: Write \(y=kx\) and decide which value must be divided by which to isolate \(k\).

questions.concept: Constant of Direct Proportionality in a Table
questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant of proportionality from a table of directly proportional values.
questions.question:
The table shows a direct proportion between \(x\) and \(y\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
x & 2 & 4 & 6\\
\hline
y & 10 & 20 & 30
\end{array}
\]
What is the constant of proportionality?
questions.explanation: In a direct proportion, the ratio \(\frac{y}{x}\) is constant. Using the first column, \(\frac{10}{2}=5\). Checking the others, \(\frac{20}{4}=5\) and \(\frac{30}{6}=5\). Therefore, the constant of proportionality is \(5\). The alternative copies the first \(y\)-value instead of calculating \(\frac{y}{x}\).
questions.hint: Check that the same ratio works for every given pair.

questions.concept: Constant of Direct Proportionality in Distance and Time
questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant of proportionality in a constant-speed distance-time relationship.
questions.question: A car travels \(240\text{ km}\) in \(4\text{ h}\) at a constant speed. The distance travelled is directly proportional to the time. What is the constant of proportionality in kilometres per hour?
questions.explanation: The rate is distance divided by time: \(k=\frac{240}{4}=60\text{ km/h}\). The alternative multiplies distance by time, \(240\times 4=960\), instead of dividing.
questions.hint: Identify which variable is the output and which is the input.

questions.concept: Constant of Direct Proportionality in Cost and Mass
questions.learningObjective: Determine the unit cost as a constant of proportionality.
questions.question: If \(5\text{ kg}\) of rice costs \(35\text{ yuan}\), and the cost is directly proportional to the mass, what is the constant of proportionality in yuan per kilogram?
questions.explanation: The cost per kilogram is \(k=\frac{35}{5}=7\text{ yuan}\) per kilogram. The alternative copies the mass instead of finding the cost per kilogram.
questions.hint: Use the units of the requested constant to decide the ratio order.

questions.concept: Constant of Direct Proportionality from a Graph Point
questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant of proportionality from a point on the graph of a direct proportion.
questions.question: The graph of a direct proportion passes through the point \((7,42)\). What is the constant of proportionality in \(y=kx\)?
questions.explanation: A point \((x,y)\) on a direct proportion satisfies \(y=kx\). Substitute \(x=7\) and \(y=42\): \(42=7k\). Dividing both sides by \(7\) gives \(k=6\). The alternative adds the coordinates, \(7+42=49\), instead of finding their ratio.
questions.hint: Read the point as an \((x,y)\) pair and substitute it into \(y=kx\).

questions.concept: Constant of Direct Proportionality with Decimal Values
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the constant of proportionality when the given values include decimals.
questions.question: If \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\), and \(y=3.5\) when \(x=0.5\), what is the constant of proportionality?
questions.explanation: For direct proportion, \(y=kx\). Substitute \(y=3.5\) and \(x=0.5\): \(3.5=0.5k\). Dividing both sides by \(0.5\) gives \(k=7\). The alternative subtracts the values, \(3.5-0.5=3\), instead of dividing.
questions.hint: Identify which variable is the output and which is the input.

questions.concept: Constant of Direct Proportionality in Cost and Quantity
questions.learningObjective: Determine the unit cost as a constant of proportionality.
questions.question: If \(12\) identical pencils cost \(9\text{ yuan}\), and the cost is directly proportional to the number of pencils, what is the constant of proportionality in yuan per pencil?
questions.explanation: The cost per pencil is \(k=\frac{9}{12}=0.75\text{ yuan}\) per pencil. The alternative reverses the ratio, giving \(\frac{12}{9}\approx 1.33\) instead of the cost per pencil.
questions.hint: Use the units of the requested constant to decide the ratio order.

questions.concept: Constant of Direct Proportionality with Decimal Values
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the constant of proportionality from decimal directly proportional values.
questions.question: The variables \(p\) and \(q\) are directly proportional, with \(p=kq\). If \(p=0.6\) when \(q=0.15\), what is \(k\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute \(p=0.6\) and \(q=0.15\) into \(p=kq\): \(0.6=k\times 0.15\). Dividing both sides by \(0.15\) gives \(k=4\). The alternative reverses the ratio, \(\frac{0.15}{0.6}=0.25\).
questions.hint: Substitute the given pair into \(p=kq\) and decide which value is divided by which.

questions.concept: Constant of Direct Proportionality from Two Points
questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant of proportionality from two points on a direct proportion.
questions.question: A direct proportion passes through the points \((4,10)\) and \((10,25)\). What is the constant of proportionality in \(y=kx\)?
questions.explanation: For a direct proportion, the ratio \(\frac{y}{x}\) is constant. Using the first point, \(\frac{10}{4}=2.5\). Checking the second point, \(\frac{25}{10}=2.5\). Therefore, the constant of proportionality is \(2.5\). The alternative reverses the ratio, \(\frac{4}{10}=0.4\).
questions.hint: Identify which variable is the output and which is the input.
